papers.title_en: Recompute or Restore? Host-Tier KV for Multi-Model Agent Workflows on a Static-Graph NPU Serving Stack
papers.evidence: 研究多模型智能体工作流中被驱逐KV前缀的恢复与重算取舍
papers.tldr: 多模型Agent工作流共享长上下文前缀，但静态图NPU设备KV预算固定，负载下被驱逐前缀只能重算。本文在Rebellions ATOM+与vllm-rbln上构建同步主机DRAM KV层，并配调度感知事件模型判断恢复是否优于重算。实验将两种过载下SLO达成率从22.8%/9.4%提升到100%/99.8%，链式与分叉负载保守增益11.8%/18.2%。模型多数延迟预测在15%内，但会误排策略并高估廉价存储路径收益，说明取舍受调度、传输与容量共同影响。
papers.abstract_en: Agent workflows issue dependent model calls that share long context prefixes, so serving them efficiently depends on reusing the key-value (KV) cache of those prefixes. On accelerators that compile model graphs ahead of time, however, the device KV budget is fixed, and prefixes evicted under load must be recomputed. Restoring them from host memory avoids this recomputation, but the transfer occupies the same engine thread as prefill and decode, so its benefit is not guaranteed. In this paper, we study when restoring beats recomputing on a commercial static-graph neural processing unit (NPU) stack (Rebellions ATOM+, vllm-rbln 0.10.2) that serves a Qwen3-8B planner on two cards and a Qwen3-0.6B executor on one. We first show that repeated prefill dominates planner work when default serving collapses: 89.5% of the executed planner prompt tokens had been materialized before. We then build a synchronous host-DRAM tier on the runtime's public KV copy calls, together with a scheduler-aware event model whose predictions are frozen before each test cohort. Experimental results show that the host tier raises workflow service-level objective (SLO) attainment from 22.8% to 100% and from 9.4% to 99.8% in the two tested overload conditions, and endpoint confirmation on two new seeds supports conservative load gains of 11.8% (chain) and 18.2% (fork), while mixed and bursty workloads remain seed-sensitive. The frozen model predicts median and 99th-percentile (P99) latency within its 15% tolerance in all 24 common-load conditions, including the 16-18% P99 increase that the tier causes for fork workflows, but it misorders three policy contrasts and overestimates the benefit of a cheaper store path (11% predicted against 3.1% measured). The trade-off therefore depends on runtime scheduling and transfer cost as well as cache capacity.

papers.title_en: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
papers.authors: Wei Feng, Meiling Chen, Boxiao Chen, Lu Liu, Bin Zi, Libin Ye, Xingyu Lu, Lei Xu, Jun Zhou
papers.evidence: 轨迹感知路由与调度促进LLM智能体工作负载的KV缓存复用
papers.tldr: LLM智能体批量任务需在推理与环境交互间交替执行，批完成时间（makespan）成为评测、合成数据与RL rollout的关键瓶颈。本文通过推理-环境协同优化：用负载资源模型分配KV缓存与循环状态，结合轨迹感知路由调度和链推进动作调度（CAAS），并引入受控回放支持消融。在BFCL、SWE-bench Multilingual、WideSearch和MCP-Atlas上，Ling-3.0/3.1-Flash使makespan降低10.4%至65.0%且评分保持一致，已用于Ling-3.x训练评测流程。
papers.abstract_en: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. Since these tasks alternate between LLM inference and environment interaction, we present coordinated optimizations to reduce batch makespan, the time required to complete all tasks in a batch. For hybrid LLMs, a workload-based resource model guides GPU-memory allocation between key-value (KV) cache and recurrent state and provides a reference sample concurrency to exploit parallelism while limiting recomputation. Trajectory-aware routing and scheduling promote cache reuse while balancing worker load. Under constrained environment capacity, we decouple sample admission from environment execution and introduce Chain-Advancing Action Scheduling (CAAS), which prioritizes long chains using observed progress to shorten the batch tail. Controlled replay combines actual inference with recorded environment responses and durations for ablations of individual optimizations. Live evaluations with Ling-3.0-Flash and Ling-3.1-Flash on the BFCL, SWE-bench Multilingual, WideSearch, and MCP-Atlas benchmarks demonstrate makespan reductions of 10.4% to 65.0%, while evaluation scores remain aligned. Furthermore, these methods have been successfully applied to training and evaluation workflows for the Ling-3.x model series, accelerating the model-development cycle.
